matches.rationale: Finding 3 directly targets Table 2 and reports that the caption admits adjusted values exaggerate AC-ViT's advantage, matching GT1's inflated noise-robustness results in Table 2.
Finding 1 identifies a Section 2.2 path-count contradiction (1024 vs 127), which corresponds to GT2's claim that path-count statements contradict the formulas shown.
No finding addresses the unequal training epochs (700 vs 300) between AC-ViT and Residual ViT.
No finding targets the Conclusion's overgeneralized universal claims about matching or outperforming residual baselines.
No finding mentions fabricated references or misdescribed prior work in the Related Work section.
No finding addresses the omission of environmental or energy implications of the longer ACN training.
Finding 7 critiques the abstract's 18% claim on absolute-vs-relative percentage grounds, whereas GT7 is about overgeneralization from specific configurations; these are different issues.
No finding discusses promotional or rhetorical exaggeration in the Introduction.
Finding 4 explicitly identifies Figure 6's caption admitting the Residual Mixer loss was obscured, matching GT9's manipulated Figure 6 curves.
Finding 8 states that detailed hyperparameter settings are omitted in Section 4.2.1, matching GT10's reproducibility concern about missing experimental protocol details.
No finding addresses overstatement of the Section 6 continual-learning result beyond the narrow Split CIFAR-100 benchmark.
No finding identifies promotional phrasing in the Abstract as an overstated rhetorical presentation issue.
No finding discusses missing fairness or bias considerations in the Discussion.
No finding identifies unequal training effort or batch sizes between ACNs and residual baselines.
No finding describes Figures 2/3 as unrealistically smooth or lacking error bars; figure-placeholder and numbering findings are different issues.
No finding relates Section 2.2's linear-backward-path claim to inconsistent experimental gradient-flow heatmaps or plots.
